extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers and policymakers interested in postwar German economic policy
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report reproducing State Department guidance and related hearings describing the standards, aims, and technical criteria for Allied reparations, industrial removals, food and fuel allocations, and administration of the German peacetime economy after World War II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad purposes for U.S. policy in Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: Our broad purposes are to ensure that our policy in Germany makes the maximum possible contribution to recovery in areas recently liberated from Germany and, positively, to set up a structure that will provide for the future recovery of Germany in conformity with the principles agreed at Potsdam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles guide four principal immediate aims (coal exports, reparations/disarmament machinery, administrative agencies, prevention of mass starvation) and a multi-stage recovery plan; policy should balance aiding liberated areas with future German recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase coal exports from Germany to liberated areas
rubrics_metrics.description: First, to increase to the greatest possible extent the export of coal from Germany to liberated areas; the rate of economic recovery in Europe depends upon the coal supplies available over this winter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This priority may delay German recovery; maximization of coal exports is in accordance with existing directives and should be pursued even at cost to German industrial output in the short term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use months before spring to set up reparations and disarmament machinery
rubrics_metrics.description: Second, to use the months before spring to set up and to set into motion, in conjunction with our allies, the machinery necessary to execute the reparations and disarmament programs laid down and agreed at Potsdam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes making clear the technical basis for reparations calculations; Allied Control Council must determine amount and character of industrial capital equipment unnecessary for peacetime economy prior to Feb. 2, 1946.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide minimum food supply; 1,550 calorie ration level
rubrics_metrics.description: A calory level for the normal German consumer has been established at 1,550 per day to avoid mass starvation; this requires substantial imports of foodstuffs, especially wheat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1,550 calories is a basic level to prevent mass starvation this winter though insufficient long-term; a higher level may be raised by agreement among the four occupying powers if justified by liberated areas' standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine industrial capital removals to eliminate German war potential
rubrics_metrics.description: The Allied Control Council's task is to eliminate German industrial capacity to produce finished arms, ammunition, implements of war, aircraft and sea‑going ships, either by removing such capacity as reparation or by destroying it, and to effectuate a drastic reduction in metallurgical, machinery and chemical industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removals are aimed at eliminating war potential and deciding reparations volume; this determination must be completed (timetable cited: before Feb. 2, 1946) and is limited in purpose, not designed to impose permanent limitations on peacetime industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid punitive destruction of capital valuable to peacetime economy
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States does not seek 'punitive destruction of capital equipment of value to the German peacetime economy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Destruction should be limited to what is necessary to eliminate war potential; non-specialized installations usable for peacetime or temporary shelter should not be wantonly destroyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destroy only specialized installations that cannot be removed
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be necessary to destroy specialized installations and structures used in shipbuilding, aircraft, armaments, explosives and certain chemicals which cannot be removed as reparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non‑specialized installations in same fields may be destroyed only if their integration substantially facilitates reconversion from peacetime to war purposes at a later date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not withhold equipment to retain remaining installations
rubrics_metrics.description: In removing equipment from plants declared available for reparation, no consideration should be given to withholding portions of the equipment desired by a reparation recipient in order to retain remaining installations and structures in peacetime uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reparation recipients' selections should not be impeded by occupying powers attempting to preserve any part of the plant for peacetime use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Berlin Declaration and geographic limits as basis for calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Berlin Declaration furnishes a guide to removals of industrial equipment; the geographical limits of Germany for these purposes are those in conformity with the Berlin Declaration (Altreich less territory east of the Oder‑Neisse line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Berlin Declaration's language (machine industry, chemical industry) should be interpreted broadly to include metal‑working and chemical sectors convertible to war production; use as general guide for removals and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base retained industrial capacity on a chosen prewar consumption standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The German standard of living chosen as a basis for estimating industrial capital equipment to remain in Germany could be arrived at by use of German consumption data in a year in which the German standard of living most closely approximated the 1930‑38 average in Europe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting the benchmark year, adjust for population changes, deviations in consumption patterns, and allow for reconstruction needs; chosen standard should aim that post‑removal capacity can produce a European‑average standard of living (excluding UK and USSR) by a target (e.g., 1948).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow specific adjustments when estimating required capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments should be made for (a) population change between the selected year and 1948, (b) notable deviations in pattern of German consumption in the selected year, (c) allowance to enable reconstruction of widespread damage to buildings and transport over a reasonable period, and (d) leave sufficient resources so Germany can exist without external assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These adjustments ensure estimates of retained capacity account for reconstruction burdens and do not require indefinite outside aid; reconstruction deficits may be spread over a multi‑year period (example: repairs over twenty years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain capacity sufficient to produce exports to pay for essential imports
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the amount of capital equipment to be retained in Germany, provision need be made for capacity to produce exports sufficient to pay for estimated current imports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No allowance should be made to provide capacity to pay for externally‑incurred occupation costs (imports consumed by occupying forces, troop pay not expended in Germany). Margins of safety unnecessary if export potential is reasonably estimated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary emphasis on agricultural and peaceful domestic industries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Berlin Declaration stipulates that primary emphasis shall be given to the development of agricultural and peaceful domestic industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum possible provision should be made for exports from sources other than metal, machinery and chemical industries to reduce risk of rearmament and promote peacetime economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourage use of removals for another country's commercial advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States is opposed to any country attempting to use the industrial capacity lost in Germany to its own commercial ends at the expense of a peacetime German economy (e.g., protecting American markets from German goods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removals should not be exploited to aid national markets or to gain 'selfish advantage'; transferred capacity is expected to replace industry destroyed by the Germans elsewhere, principally in Europe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupying authorities should set conditions for German self‑management
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up German administrative agencies which would operate under close policy control of the occupying authorities in the fields of finance, transport, communications, foreign trade and industry so Germany can be treated as an economic unit and move toward recovery and termination of military occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Development of interzonal and international trade machinery, common policies in transport, agriculture, banking, currency, taxation, and completion of denazification are prerequisites for Germans to assume responsibility for their economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus immediate activity on transport, housing, utilities, coal and agriculture
rubrics_metrics.description: Military government should concentrate on the repair of transport, emergency repair of housing and essential utilities and the maximization of coal and agricultural production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These repairs and maximization efforts are critical to prevent mass starvation and to enable any later selective industrial reactivation; some coal must remain in Germany for minimum repairs even while exports are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey fuel and raw material needs and prioritize selective reactivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Military government authorities should survey the fuel and raw material requirements of German industries capable of supplying essential civilian goods and of manufacturing for export so that a program for selective reactivation of remaining industrial capacity can get under way when coal and raw materials permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority should be given to industries which, relative to fuel and raw material expenditure, will contribute most toward striking an ultimate export‑import balance and satisfy pressing internal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupying powers may need to finance minimum imports to prevent disease and unrest
rubrics_metrics.description: Under conditions where exports from stocks and current production do not suffice, the United States and other occupying powers may have to finance minimum imports into Germany necessary to prevent disease and unrest endangering occupying forces and to reactivate selected export industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is tied to the 'disease and unrest' formula; occupying powers' responsibility is to provide reasonable opportunity for attainment of balance at minimum standard of living though they are not obliged to provide full living standard during occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased economic recovery approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize stages of recovery: immediate phase (prevent starvation, maximize coal exports to liberated areas, emergency repairs), a second stage (set up reparations/disarmament machinery and administrative agencies, selective reactivation), and a third stage following reparation removals when Germany regains more control over its economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and allocations (coal, food, equipment removals) should be planned with these stages in mind; staged reviews (e.g., next spring) determine when to reallocate coal for domestic industrial production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of living goal after removals (not above European average)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Berlin Declaration is interpreted to mean Germany's industrial capacity after reparation removals should be physically capable of producing a standard of living equivalent to the European average (excluding the United Kingdom and the USSR) in the period following the two‑year reparations removals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department of State views the Declaration as not intended to force a reduction in German living standards except as required to enable reparations payments; practical production may lag and adjustments are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit removals so Germany can export enough to pay essential imports
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States should not approve removals on such a scale that Germany would be unable, owing to shortage of capital equipment, to export goods in sufficient quantities to pay for essential imports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capacity must be left to enable exports to yield foreign exchange for imports required for the agreed minimum standard of living; safety margins can be provided via reconstruction timeframes rather than extra capacity.
